catalog_quote: Mocho' stress is regular and falls on the last syllable of the word. The primary correlate of stress in Mocho' is falling pitch for long marked tone vowels and peak (high) pitch of the word for short vowels and plain long vowels, which is further described in the following sections. Although stressed syllables may have increased relative intensity, differences in loudness are difficult to identify or perceive. Stressed syllables are also often lengthened, but length is more difficult to perceive as length modulation is also manipulated to show affect. Although stress is described in the scope of single-word stress, the realm of stress marking extends to the phonological phrase that can include one or more “words” as traditionally defined. ... [Sec. 3.4, p. 97] Mocho' has word-final stress and phrase-final intonational stress that correlates with rising pitch. Long vowels with falling pitch are found only in word-final position.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (including suffixes: adding a suffix moves stress onto it). Mocho' also has an incipient tone contrast (falling vs. plain pitch on long vowels) that is licensed only in the stressed, i.e. word-final, syllable and is neutralized elsewhere.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; no mention of secondary stress found in the dissertation.
new_statements.exceptions: No lexical exceptions stated for native vocabulary ('regular'). Spanish loans: early loans adapted to final stress/high pitch; later (Stage 2/3) loans may retain Spanish non-final stress, with falling-pitch long vowels appearing in the Spanish stressed syllable (Ch. 4, Sec. on hispanisms). Falling tone on a root is lost when a suffix takes the stress (e.g. pò:x 'medicine' vs po:x-o:m 'curer'; tà:nh 'lime' possessed).
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word (root plus suffixes; possessive/agentive suffixes attract the stress), with the author noting that stress marking extends to the phonological phrase and that there is additionally phrase-final intonational stress (Sec. 3.4: 'Mocho' has word-final stress and phrase-final intonational stress that correlates with rising pitch'). Evidence is from elicited citation forms with pitch tracks (Figs. 2.1-2.27). Describes Mocho' of Motozintla; closely related Tuzanteco treated separately in 3.2.4 (has lost length/tone).
new_statements.identity_note: Palosaari 2011 describes Mocho' as spoken in Motozintla de Mendoza, Chiapas, Mexico (glottocode moch1257, ISO mhc; older names Motozintleco, Cotoque). The closely related Tuzanteco variety (Tuzantán) is discussed separately (Sec. 3.2.4) and differs prosodically (has lost vowel length and lacks the tone contrast); the stress statement applies to Mocho' proper.

tone_statements.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Ryan Bennett. 2020. Mesoamerica. In Carlos Gussenhoven & Aoju Chen (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody, 407-427. Oxford: Oxford University Press. doi:10.1093/oxfordhb/9780198832232.013.25 (open postprint: eScholarship UC Santa Cruz qt6xh4n935, chapter 27 'Prosodic Systems: Mesoamerica').
tone_statements.quote: Lexical tone is also attested in Southern Lacandon (Yucatecan), Uspanteko (Eastern Mayan), Mocho’ (Western Mayan), and possibly one variety of Tsotsil ... Palosaari (2011) describes nouns in Mocho’ as having a three-way contrast in stressed, final syllables between toneless long vowels (e.g. kaanh [ˈkaːŋ] ‘four’), long vowels with falling tone (marked as low, e.g. kaanh [kàːŋ] ‘sky’), and toneless short vowels (e.g. k’anh [ˈkˀaŋ] ‘loud’) (see also Martin 1984).
tone_statements.locator: sec. 27.3.2 'Lexical tone', postprint ms p. 11 and ms p. 12 (published chapter pp. 407-427)
tone_statements.summary: Survey, second-hand (Palosaari 2011): Mocho' tonal; privative falling (written low) vs toneless, only on long vowels in stressed final syllables. Tuzantec (a dialect?) called incipient/quasi-tonemic.

tone_statements.citation: Palosaari Fox, Naomi. 2008. Tonogenesis: evidence from Mocho'. Paper presented at the [11th] Workshop on American Indian [= Indigenous] Languages (WAIL), University of California, Santa Barbara, May 23-25, 2008. Unpublished; not in the WAIL 11 proceedings (Santa Barbara Papers in Linguistics 19, 2008) as listed on linguistics.ucsb.edu.
tone_statements.quote: A tonal contrast has been proposed for Mocho' long vowels (Campbell 1988; Martin 1984; Palosaari Fox 2008). The tonal contrast is correlated with stress, as long vowels with falling pitch are only found in stressed syllables. ... Falling pitch is considered marked because it is limited in distribution ... Falling pitch is only found in syllables in stressed position and is neutralized in any other position ... The pitch contrast is, therefore, only found in nominals ... The pitch contrast is lexically distinctive, as multiple minimal pairs can be found
tone_statements.summary: Marginal contrast: falling (grave-marked) vs plain long vowels, only in the stressed word-final syllable of nominals, neutralized when suffixed; reflex of PM *VʔC. Praat pitch tracks + minimal pairs.

sources.note: Sec. 2.3.1 (p. 34): 'Mocho' stress is regular and falls on the last syllable of the word.' Primary correlate is pitch (peak/high pitch on stressed short and plain long vowels; falling pitch on marked-tone long vowels); falling-pitch (tonal) long vowels occur only in stressed = word-final syllables and are neutralized when a suffix takes the stress (pò:x vs po:x-o:m; mì:m vs possessed form); stress marking extends to the phonological phrase; Sec. 3.4: 'Mocho' has word-final stress and phrase-final intonational stress'.

tone.quote: The forms Kaufman represents as CVˀC are almost never pronounced with a full glottal stop. Rather, most frequently they have a long vowel with falling pitch, written here as /CV̂:C/. However, this correspondence is not uniform; some forms given by Kaufman as CVˀC have no falling pitch, and other forms (especially those with ŋ) have falling pitch but are not CVˀC in Kaufman's dictionary. These CVˀC or CV̂:C forms are the most problematical in my data, and they should be reinvestigated with much more attention.
